rulings.challenge_claim: The boundary_rationale overstates continuous rejoice/remember interleaving across v.7-10 and omits the undisclosed cross-seam imperative pairing bearing on where the aging-allegory wisdom_poem zone actually begins.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from bytes (byte tier for all splices below, spliced from source, re-collated). Root zayin-kaf-resh (remember) is word-bound-swept at exactly 7 verses book-wide (skeleton tier: Eccl.1.11, 2.16, 5.19, 9.5, 9.15, 11.8, 12.1 -- LF's own digit, re-verified); within the row's own v.7-10 span it occurs ONLY at v.8, not repeated at v.9 or v.10, so "interleave continuously across v.7-10" is byte-false as an internal-cohesion claim (rejoice does repeat, at v.8 and v.9, sweep: 14 verses book-wide skeleton tier, re-verified -- but remember does not). Separately, an undisclosed 2ms-imperative chain crosses the row's own closing seam unbroken: שְׂמַ֧ח (v.9) / וְהָסֵ֥ר (v.10) / וּזְכֹר֙ (12:1) are all rendered as imperatives by WEB (Rejoice.../Therefore remove.../Remember also...). The youth phrase בִּימֵ֣י בְחוּרוֹתֶ֔ךָ (11:9) recurs near-identically as בִּימֵ֖י בְּחוּרֹתֶ֑יךָ (12:1) -- word-bound skeleton sweep of that two-word construction: exactly 2 verses, 11:9 and 12:1. Neither device is disclosed on this row's own closing-seam side. This bears on the wisdom_poem's owner-named default zone (11:9-12:7, book_strategy Eccl.md §6), whose exact bounds are explicitly writer-argued, not owner-fixed.
rulings.remedy: Correct the internal cohesion claim to name the actual per-root counts within v.7-10 (rejoice repeats, remember does not) rather than asserting undifferentiated "interleaving." Add explicit disclosure in boundary_rationale or device_notes of the imperative chain and youth-phrase catchword crossing the 11.10|12.1 seam, and state why the row still closes at v.10 despite that continuity (or move the boundary if the writer concludes otherwise) -- the cure test is that a reviewer re-checking v.7-10 for interleaving finds the row's own claim matches the count, and that the crossing device is named and addressed rather than silent.

rulings.challenge_claim: The 11:8 gloss misreads a conditional protasis as a jussive and marks a nonexistent gap in a contiguous byte run; the rejoice/remember interleave the row names as cohesion warrant is truncated one verse short of its own closing seam, where two byte-true devices cross undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: Two components, ruled separately. (1) Jussive-mood component UPHELD: WEB's own rendering of 11:8, which the row cites as its match, treats the leading verb as the protasis of a ki-im conditional ("if a man lives many years") and only the two verbs that follow (rejoice, remember) as jussive-like ("let him rejoice... but let him remember"). The row's rough gloss "let the man live... let him rejoice" casts the protasis verb as a parallel jussive, which the row's own paired WEB citation does not support -- a real mood-attribution defect. (2) "Nonexistent gap" framing NOT UPHELD as an independent defect: the row's Hebrew splice is the full contiguous 4-word run (byte-verified, spliced-and-recollated), and ellipsis inside a straight-quoted rough gloss (as opposed to the curly-quoted verbatim WEB text) is this corpus's own standing convention elsewhere in the same cluster (e.g. row P03-026's gloss of oshb:Eccl.12.1, "before...not"); no reader is misled about Hebrew contiguity by it. (3) Cross-seam cohesion UPHELD and CONVERGENT with the LF item on this same row: word-bound sweep confirms the remember-root pairing at exactly 2 verses in the zone (11:8, 12:1), the youth-phrase catchword at exactly 2 verses (11:9, 12:1, consonantal skeleton identical apart from the pronominal suffix), and an unbroken 2ms-imperative chain from 11:9 through 11:10 into 12:1 (all WEB-rendered as imperatives) -- all crossing the row's own closing seam without disclosure. This is the same underlying defect LF's item on this row identifies, reached via additional, independently confirmed evidence (the youth catchword).
rulings.remedy: Re-cut the rough gloss at 11:8 so the protasis verb is not rendered as a jussive parallel to the two verbs that follow. Add the imperative-chain/youth-catchword disclosure per the LF item's remedy on this same row -- one edit can address both.

rulings.grounds: Mirrors the P03-025/LF finding from the poem's own opening side, re-verified independently: the aging-allegory wisdom_poem's owner-named default zone is 11:9-12:7 (book_strategy Eccl.md §6), yet this row's boundary_rationale supplies internal-spine evidence for the poem (the triple ad-asher-lo anaphora, sweep: 3 verses -- 12:1, 12:2, 12:6, re-verified byte tier) and its terminus at 12:7, but no evidence for its own OPENING seam at 11.10|12.1. The same crossing devices found on the P03-025 side apply here undisclosed: the 2ms-imperative chain שְׂמַ֧ח/וְהָסֵ֥ר/וּזְכֹר֙ and the youth-phrase catchword בִּימֵ֣י בְחוּרוֹתֶ֔ךָ <-> בִּימֵ֖י בְּחוּרֹתֶ֑יךָ (word-bound skeleton sweep: 2 verses each). The row's disclosed rejected_alternative (splitting v.1-7 into three rows at the anaphora sites) is an internal-structure question and does not address this external, uncited rival.
rulings.remedy: Add explicit disclosure of the crossing imperative chain and youth-catchword to boundary_rationale or device_notes, and state why the wisdom_poem's own default start (11:9 per §6) is not adopted here -- or adopt it, if the writer's byte-argument favors that. Either resolution cures the gap provided it is argued from the disclosed bytes; this is the same single cure as the P03-025/LF and P03-025/OL items on the adjacent row (one edit, applied on both sides of the seam, can close all three).

rulings.challenge_claim: The 12:6 ketiv/qere is described as one uncommon verb when the two witnesses' consonantal forms are two different roots and the single gloss fits neither arm cleanly, and the row's asserted opening boundary at 12:1 carries no Hebrew evidence while a byte-true catchword crosses it.
rulings.grounds: Both components re-derived and confirmed. (1) Ketiv/qere: the pmarks K/Q inventory carries exactly 1 note at MT 12:6. The ketiv ירחק and qere יֵרָתֵק֙ are two DIFFERENT consonantal roots (resh-het-qof vs resh-tav-qof, differing in the middle radical), not one verb pointed two ways: word-bound skeleton sweep of the ketiv's root returns 2 verses book-wide (3:5, 12:6), while the qere's root returns exactly 1 verse book-wide (12:6 only, a hapax reading). The row's "on the uncommon 'loosed' verb" phrasing describes this as a single lexeme, which the bytes do not support. (2) Opening-seam gap: same undisclosed crossing catchword/imperative chain identified in the LF item on this row and both P03-025 items -- confirmed convergent, same underlying defect, viewed from the ketiv/qere angle plus the shared seam-disclosure gap.
rulings.remedy: Correct the ketiv/qere characterization to name both roots rather than one lexeme, disclosing which sense each arm supports as an openly-held crux (consistent with this zone's already-flagged low-confidence status in device_notes). Apply the same opening-seam disclosure remedy as the LF item on this row.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row argues its opening seam (spelling shift at 12.8|12.9) and its internal seam (v.11) but offers no boundary evidence for its own closing seam at 12.11|12.12, leaving a repeated verse-initial opener shared with the next row undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: Underlying defect UPHELD, evidentiary digit REFINED. The verse-initial connective וְיֹתֵ֕ר (12:9) and וְיֹתֵ֥ר מֵהֵ֖מָּה (12:12, first word) do share a root, and the closing-seam gap (no boundary_evidence_refs entry past v.11) is real -- confirmed, boundary_evidence_refs for this row cites only 12:9 and 12:11. But LF's own citation ("2 of only 13 book-wide skeleton occurrences of the root") blends two distinct objects under one digit, which the corpus's own count-discipline rule forbids: a contiguous-skeleton substring sweep on that root returns 13 verses, but 9 of those are the DIFFERENT profit/advantage noun family (e.g. יִּתְר֖וֹן at 1:3, and similar forms at 2:11, 5:8), not the more/moreover adverbial connective the row actually shares with 12:12. The precise word-bound form matching the shared connective (with the vav-prefix, as at 12:9/12:12) returns exactly 3 verses book-wide (7:11, 12:9, 12:12) -- still establishing the same undisclosed cross-seam link, just at the correctly-named object.
rulings.remedy: Disclose the shared verse-initial connective with 12:12 in boundary_rationale or device_notes, and state why the unit still closes at v.11 (e.g. because the connective functions as a discourse-serial linker rather than a cohesion signal, if that is the writer's judgment). Cite the connective count as its own object (word-bound form, not the blended root) if a digit is used.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row calls a mid-verse splice the unit's opening and omits 12:9's actual verse-initial connective, which is the epilogue's own serial linker and the strongest byte signal bearing on this very seam, while the spelling leg it does cite is inert.
rulings.grounds: All three components confirmed from bytes. (1) 12:9 opens with וְיֹתֵ֕ר, not with the row's cited splice-start word; WEB's own rendering opens "Further," reflecting that word, and the row's curly-quoted WEB excerpt ("because the Preacher was wise...") begins after it -- both the Hebrew splice and its paired WEB quote skip the true opening word. (2) That same connective form recurs verse-initially at 12:12 (וְיֹתֵ֥ר מֵהֵ֖מָּה, first word) -- word-bound sweep of the exact form: 3 verses book-wide (7:11, 12:9, 12:12) -- an epilogue-spanning serial linker crossing both this row's own opening seam and the P03-029 row's opening seam, undisclosed on either side. (3) The spelling-contrast argument (defective qohelet spelling at 12:9-10 vs. the plene-definite form הַקּוֹהֶ֖לֶת-pattern at 12:8) is factually correct but inert as fresh boundary evidence here: the defective spelling is the book's ordinary form at 6 of the name's 7 sites, so its mere presence at 12:9 does not discriminate a new unit -- it already did its boundary work establishing 12:8's uniqueness and cannot carry the 12:8|12:9 seam a second time.
rulings.remedy: Re-cut the row's opening Hebrew splice and WEB quote to begin at the true verse-initial connective, disclosing the link to 12:12. Replace or supplement the spelling-contrast rationale, since it is not independent evidence for this seam.

rulings.challenge_claim: The stated opening is again a mid-verse splice -- 12:12 actually opens with a waw-conjunctive plus an anaphoric back-reference to the preceding verse -- and the row's 'book's final imperative' is byte-false, since another imperative follows it in the same verse.
rulings.grounds: Both components UPHELD from bytes; severity corrected upward. (1) 12:12 opens with וְיֹתֵ֥ר מֵהֵ֖מָּה -- a waw-conjunctive plus an anaphoric "than these," pointing back at the 12:11 material -- not with the vocative caution בְּנִ֣י הִזָּהֵ֑ר as the row's Hebrew splice and WEB quote both claim; confirmed by direct byte inspection, the same mid-verse-splice-labeled-as-opening pattern found in the P03-028/OL item. (2) "Book's final imperative": byte-false. 12:13 reads אֶת הָאֱלֹהִ֤ים יְרָא֙ ... וְאֶת מִצְוֺתָ֣יו שְׁמ֔וֹר -- "fear God ... and keep his commandments" -- and שְׁמ֔וֹר is itself an imperative, standing AFTER the fear-God imperative in the same verse; 12:14 contains no imperative in either witness. The book's actual final imperative is שְׁמ֔וֹר, not the fear-God phrase the row names. SEVERITY REFINED from low to medium: this is not only an under-argued boundary but a flat misstatement of the verse's own grammatical content, independent of any boundary question.
rulings.remedy: Re-cut the opening Hebrew splice/WEB quote to begin at the verse-initial connective, disclosing the backward anaphora to 12:11 (same pattern-fix as the P03-028/OL item). Correct "the book's final imperative" to name שְׁמ֔וֹר (12:13), or drop the "final imperative" characterization if not needed for the row's argument.
